svg.aria-label: Four steps of tRNA processing and the two routes of RNA editing: RNase P cutting the 5-prime end as a ribozyme, templateless CCA addition providing the amino acid attachment site, the anticodon inosine, and cytosine to uracil editing of apolipoprotein B producing two protein lengths in different tissues.
svg.text: A tRNA processing: four steps
mature tRNA region
extra 5'
extra 3'
1 RNase P cuts the 5' end
RNase P is RNA plus protein, and the catalytic part
is the RNA: it is a ribozyme
2 the extra 3' region is trimmed
3 CCA is added to the 3' end
... C C A - 3'OH
not encoded in the genome; added without a template
the amino acid attaches to this final 3'-OH
4 bases are modified
dihydrouridine, pseudouridine, inosine, methyl derivatives
inosine at the first anticodon position pairs with several bases,
so one tRNA reads more than one codon
some tRNA genes carry an intron, but the spliceosome
does not remove it: a dedicated endonuclease and ligase do
B RNA editing changes single bases
splicing
removes a segment and joins what remains
editing
swaps one base for another, one residue at a time
the transcript no longer matches the genome, so genomic
sequence alone cannot predict the protein
C to U deamination: apolipoprotein B
C
liver
codon read as glutamine, translation continues
full-length ApoB-100
U
small intestine
that codon becomes a stop codon
truncated ApoB-48
A to I deamination (ADAR): inosine is read as guanosine, so codons change; frequent in the nervous system
